newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW-Eastern Water sees strong Thai debut.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Eastern Water sees strong Thai debut.

text.p: Thai utility firm Eastern Water Resources Development and Management expects its shares to make a strong debut on the bourse later this month on brighter market sentiment after strong foreign demand following the floating of the baht.
"We are very confident that our shares will make a strong debut," its president Wanchai Ghooprasert told Reuters in an interview.
Eastern Water expects its listing application on the Stock Exchange of Thailand to be approved by the end of July, Wanchai said.
"Apart from the company's sound fundamentals, the significant improvement in market sentiment would help support our shares," he said.
Thailand's stock market has rallied by over 20 percent since the baht's flotation on Wednesday
The Bank of Thailand ended months of devaluation speculation by floating the currency after a 13-year peg to a basket of currencies dominated by the dollar.
The move which was seen as a de facto devaluation saw the baht lose around 15-20 percent of its value and sparked stampede for Thai stocks by foreign investors, brokers said.
Strong demand from investors who failed to subscribe to Eastern Water shares during the initial public offering (IPO) last month would also help boost share prices, he said.
Eastern Water shares have been oversubscribed 13 and six times respectively by international and local investors during its IPO last month, he said.
The company had offered 51 million shares at 30 baht each.
Wanchai said Eastern Water will use 2.0 billion baht in funds from the IPO to expand its water supply network and to develop new water storage facilities.
"We expect the demand for water in the area to grow by about 25 percent over the next five years. So we have to develop the new water saviour to keep pace with those demand," he said.
Eastern Water is projected to post a net profit of 224 million baht ($8 million) in 1997 ended September 30. In the first six months ended March, it had a profit of 120 million baht.
"From our performance in the first six months, I am very confident that the company's profit this year will meet our earlier forecast," Wanchai said.
Eastern Water is establised under a scheme to privatise state utility agencies.
The company which is operator of water services for mainly the industrial community in eastern Thailand is majorily owned by the state-owned Provincial Waterworks Authority.
